name: app-bar
title: App bar
summary: Names the current screen at its top edge and holds the way back and the screen's most used actions, its bottom edge drawn as the edge of a region that stays (or, where the design system chooses, only once content scrolls under it).

anatomy.description: The bar across the top of the screen. Its color reaches under the system inset above it (status bar, camera cutout, window caption).
The navigation item: one icon-only Button at the start (back, menu or close). The product's icon-only Button, not restyled by the bar.

The product's brand: one link to its first page (or one image), after the navigation item, in a cell as large as an icon button's. It draws one image, the symbol alone, the wordmark alone, the symbol and the wordmark side by side (lockup), or one of the two by the window's width (responsive).
The product's context: one control after the brand (a workspace, a project, a design system), the product's own Button, not restyled by the bar.
The screen's name. In the top row for a small bar; under the top row for an expanded large bar, moving into the top row as it collapses.
One line under the title: context for it (an account, a status, when it was edited).
The action items: up to three icon-only Buttons at the end. The product's icon-only Buttons, not restyled by the bar.
The bar's bottom edge. In the default system it is drawn at rest and while content is under the bar; dividerVisibility scroll draws it only once content has scrolled under the bar.

props.name: size
props.description: Small puts the title in the one row the bar has; large gives the title a larger row of its own under the top row, which collapses into the top row as the content scrolls. One product uses small on most screens and large on its top-level ones. A design system may add values.

props.name: title
props.description: The screen's name, and the heading of the screen for assistive technology.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: One line under the title. Empty draws none.

props.name: titleAlignment
props.description: Where the title sits in the top row: after the navigation button, or centered on the bar. An expanded large bar's own title row always starts at the start.

props.name: brandHref
props.description: The address of the product's first page: the brand is a link to it. Empty draws the brand as an image that is not a link.

props.name: brandLabel
props.description: The product's name: the brand's one accessible name, whichever of its images is shown. Required wherever the bar has a brand.

props.name: brandLayout
props.description: How the brand's symbol and wordmark stand when the product gives both (APB-21): lockup sets them side by side, comp.app-bar.brand.lockup.gap apart and aligned as comp.app-bar.brand.lockup.alignment says; responsive shows the wordmark while the window is medium or wider and the symbol while it is compact, never both. One image, a symbol alone or a wordmark alone is shown as it is, at every width, under either value.

props.name: scrolled
props.description: Whether content lies under the bar. A scrolling view connected to the bar sets it (see platforms); a product without one sets it itself. It selects the bar's scrolled condition, and a large bar is drawn collapsed while it is true.

props.name: dividerVisibility
props.description: When the bar's bottom edge is drawn. always: at rest and while content is under the bar, so that the edge of the screen's header stands still (an app shell's header, a screen whose content starts right under the bar). scroll: only while content lies under the bar, so that the line itself says the content has moved (the scrolled condition's edge alone). auto takes comp.app-bar.outline.visibility, the design system's answer (always in the default system). The bar's color and elevation follow scrolled under either choice.

items.name: navigation
items.summary: The one icon-only Button at the start of the top row (back, menu or close): a Button of the text variant and the medium size with an icon and no label, unless the product sets otherwise, placed in the navigation slot, which the bar lays out and does not restyle.

props.name: label
props.description: Its accessible name ("Back"), as the Button's label. Required.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Its glyph, as the Button's icon slot. A fixture item's content is this glyph.

events.name: click
events.description: The button was activated, as the Button's click.

items.name: action
items.summary: An icon-only Button at the end of the top row, up to three in reading order: a Button of the text variant and the medium size with an icon and no label, unless the product sets otherwise, placed in the actions slot, which the bar lays out and does not restyle.

props.name: label
props.description: Its accessible name ("Search"), as the Button's label. Required.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Its glyph, as the Button's icon slot. A fixture item's content is this glyph.

events.name: click
events.description: The button was activated, as the Button's click.

slots.name: navigation
slots.description: Holds the navigation item: one icon-only Button at the start.

slots.name: brand
slots.description: The brand as one image: a product's single logo file, drawn comp.app-bar.brand.image.height high. Takes the place of brand-symbol and brand-wordmark where both are given.

slots.name: brand-symbol
slots.description: The brand's symbol: comp.app-bar.brand.symbol.size high alone, or while the window is compact under brandLayout responsive; comp.app-bar.brand.lockup.symbol.size high (the wordmark's height) beside the wordmark in a lockup.

slots.name: brand-wordmark
slots.description: The brand's wordmark, drawn comp.app-bar.brand.wordmark.height high: alone at every width, after the symbol in a lockup, or while the window is medium or wider under brandLayout responsive.

slots.name: context
slots.description: Holds one control of the product's context after the brand: a Button, or a Button that opens a Menu, that says and changes the workspace, the project or the design system the screen is in. The product's own control, not restyled by the bar.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Holds the action items, up to three icon-only Buttons at the end, in reading order; more belong in an overflow menu the product provides.

behavior.text: WHILE scrolled is false THE app bar SHALL fill its container with comp.app-bar.flat.container.color, raise it by comp.app-bar.flat.container.elevation and draw its bottom edge comp.app-bar.outline.width thick: in comp.app-bar.scrolled.outline.color WHILE its divider visibility (APB-18) is always, so that the edge stands still whether or not content lies under the bar, and in comp.app-bar.flat.outline.color WHILE it is scroll.

WHILE scrolled is true THE app bar SHALL fill its container with comp.app-bar.scrolled.container.color, raise it by comp.app-bar.scrolled.container.elevation and draw its bottom edge comp.app-bar.outline.width thick in comp.app-bar.scrolled.outline.color, under either divider visibility (APB-18).

WHEN scrolled changes THE app bar SHALL change its container color, elevation and bottom edge over comp.app-bar.motion.condition-duration with comp.app-bar.motion.condition-easing, and at once where motion is reduced; WHILE its divider visibility (APB-18) is always the bottom edge SHALL NOT change.

THE app bar SHALL span the full width of its parent and lay out a top row at least comp.app-bar.container.height.small high: the navigation item comp.app-bar.container.padding-inline from the start edge, the title block, and the action items comp.app-bar.container.padding-inline from the end edge, with comp.app-bar.container.gap between them and comp.app-bar.actions.gap between two actions, each vertically centered in the row; a navigation item SHALL go to the start and action items to the end wherever they stand among the items; WHILE there is no navigation item the title block SHALL start comp.app-bar.title.inset from the start edge, and WHILE there are no action items it SHALL end comp.app-bar.title.inset from the end edge. Right-to-left layouts SHALL mirror the order.

THE app bar SHALL draw a title in the top row on one line in comp.app-bar.title.typescale.small and comp.app-bar.title.color, and WHILE subtitle is not empty the subtitle on one line below it in comp.app-bar.subtitle.typescale.small and comp.app-bar.subtitle.color, the two vertically centered as a block; each SHALL be truncated at the end with an ellipsis when it does not fit. THE app bar SHALL set the title's letter-spacing, in every size, by the script of its text, as every title is set (PRS-20): no negative letter-spacing WHERE its language is Chinese, Japanese or Korean, and none WHERE its script joins its letters or stacks marks on them.

WHILE titleAlignment is center THE app bar SHALL center the top row's title block on the bar's full width and narrow it equally on both sides, truncating its text, so that it never overlaps the navigation or actions slots, and SHALL center its text; WHILE titleAlignment is start THE app bar SHALL start the title block after the navigation slot (or at comp.app-bar.title.inset) with its text start-aligned.

WHILE size is large and the bar is expanded THE app bar SHALL be at least comp.app-bar.container.height.large high, SHALL draw no title in its top row, and SHALL draw below the top row the title in comp.app-bar.title.typescale.large and, WHILE subtitle is not empty, the subtitle in comp.app-bar.subtitle.typescale.large, both starting comp.app-bar.title.inset from the start edge, each on one line truncated at the end, the block ending comp.app-bar.container.padding-block-end above the bar's bottom edge.

WHILE size is large and a scrolling view is connected THE app bar SHALL shrink by the distance the content has scrolled from its top, one for one, from its expanded height to comp.app-bar.container.height.small, the expanded title block moving up with the bar's bottom edge and clipped under the top row; the top row's title SHALL be invisible while the expanded title is wholly visible, fully visible once the bar has collapsed, and in between fade in linearly with the part of the expanded title that is covered. WHEN the content scrolls back toward its top THE app bar SHALL expand the same way.

WHERE a scrolling view is connected THE app bar SHALL take scrolled from it: true while any content lies under the bar (for a large bar, only once it has fully collapsed) and false when the content is at its top. WHILE size is large and scrolled is true THE app bar SHALL be drawn fully collapsed; WHERE nothing is connected and scrolled is false a large app bar SHALL stay expanded.

THE app bar SHALL extend its container under the top system inset (status bar, camera cutout, window caption) and SHALL place its content below that inset and inside the left and right insets, so that its color reaches the screen's top edge while no content sits under a system bar or cutout.

THE app bar SHALL NOT restyle its navigation and action items: each SHALL render as the icon-only Button it is, from its own tokens, and keep its own semantics, and the app bar SHALL NOT be focusable itself, so that focus moves from the navigation item to the action items in reading order. A glyph of an item that the system's icon set marks as mirrored (a navigation item's arrow_back) SHALL be mirrored in a right-to-left layout by the item's own icon helper (BTN-19): that is the icon's own behaviour, not a restyling by the app bar.

THE app bar SHALL expose title as a heading and subtitle as text read after it, and SHALL expose the title only once WHILE size is large: the expanded title while any of it is visible, the top row's title once the bar has collapsed.

WHILE title is empty THE app bar SHALL draw no title block (an expanded large bar then has an empty title row) and SHALL expose no heading; IF the app bar holds more than three action items or more than one navigation item THE app bar SHALL still render them, and in debug builds report that the extra actions belong in an overflow menu or that a bar has one navigation button.
WHEN size names a value that the active design system does not have THE app bar SHALL render with the default value's tokens, and in debug builds report the unknown value.

WHILE the text size is enlarged THE app bar SHALL grow its rows to hold the title and subtitle lines (its heights are minimums), SHALL keep each on one line truncated at the end, and SHALL NOT scale the navigation and action items it holds.

THE app bar SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the app bar is shown THE app bar SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its size and the scroll state it follows.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render. On the web the test is owed with the other right-to-left tests.

behavior.text: THE app bar SHALL lay out its title and its subtitle as text of its own direction, isolated from the text around it: each takes the base direction of its first strong character, or the layout direction where it has none, so that a left-to-right word, a number with its sign or unit, a telephone number and an address keep their own order in a right-to-left layout and reorder nothing beside them; THE app bar SHALL still place each and align its lines by the layout direction, not by the text's own, and SHALL cut a title or a subtitle that does not fit (APB-5, APB-7) at the end of its own direction, so that a left-to-right label in a right-to-left layout loses its right end and never its beginning.

THE app bar SHALL draw its bottom edge (APB-1, APB-2) as its dividerVisibility names: WHILE dividerVisibility is auto, as comp.app-bar.outline.visibility names, which follows sys.behavior.divider-visibility unless a design system sets the app bar apart; WHILE dividerVisibility is always or scroll, as that value names, whatever the tokens say. WHEN dividerVisibility, or the token it follows, changes THE app bar SHALL draw the other form at once, moving no part and keeping the scroll position and focus; WHEN dividerVisibility names a value the app bar does not define THE app bar SHALL treat it as auto and in debug builds report the unknown value. A platform that cannot draw a choice SHALL fall back to the first value, always, and state that in its README.
behavior.verify: Under the default system every fixture draws the hairline bottom edge at rest: small and small-scrolled differ in nothing the default system paints. With divider-visibility="scroll" small draws no edge and small-scrolled draws it. Under m3-like and cupertino (scroll) the representative fixtures draw what they drew before.

behavior.text: WHERE the product gives the app bar a brand (an image in brand, brand-symbol or brand-wordmark) THE app bar SHALL place it at the start of the top row, after the navigation item at comp.app-bar.actions.gap from it, or comp.app-bar.container.padding-inline from the start edge WHILE no navigation item is drawn, with the title block after it at comp.app-bar.container.gap; the brand SHALL take a cell at least the minimum target high and wide, padded at its start and end by half the minimum target less comp.app-bar.brand.symbol.size, its images centred on the row's centre line, so that a symbol stands where an icon button's icon stands and a wordmark keeps that inset from the cell's edges. Right-to-left layouts SHALL mirror the order.
behavior.verify: small-brand-symbol: the cell starts actions.gap after the navigation button, is as large as it, and the symbol's box is the navigation icon's box moved by the cell's offset. small-brand-wordmark: the wordmark starts at the same inset. Without a navigation item, or with one that is not drawn, the cell starts container.padding-inline from the start edge. In rtl the order mirrors.

behavior.text: THE app bar SHALL draw the image in brand comp.app-bar.brand.image.height high, the symbol comp.app-bar.brand.symbol.size high and the wordmark comp.app-bar.brand.wordmark.height high, each as wide as its own proportions make it, and SHALL give the brand comp.app-bar.brand.color, which an image drawn in the current color takes and an image of its own colors keeps. WHILE the brand is a lockup THE app bar SHALL draw the symbol and then the wordmark in one row, comp.app-bar.brand.lockup.gap apart, aligned in the row's block axis as comp.app-bar.brand.lockup.alignment names (center, start or end).
behavior.verify: Each image's height is its token's; a mark in currentColor is drawn in on-surface in light and dark; small-brand-lockup draws the symbol, then the wordmark lockup.gap after it, centred; setting lockup.alignment to end aligns their bottoms.

behavior.text: WHERE the brand holds one image, a symbol alone or a wordmark alone THE app bar SHALL show it at every window width. WHERE it holds both a symbol and a wordmark, WHILE brandLayout is lockup THE app bar SHALL show both as a lockup (APB-20), and WHILE brandLayout is responsive THE app bar SHALL show the wordmark WHILE the window class is medium or expanded and the symbol WHILE it is compact, never both: the window class of the app shell the bar stands in, or, outside one, the window's width against sys.breakpoint.medium. WHEN the window class changes THE app bar SHALL show the other at once, without a motion of its own, the brand's link and its focus unchanged.
behavior.verify: small-brand, small-brand-symbol and small-brand-wordmark show their image at 390 and 1440; small-brand-lockup shows both at both widths; small-brand-responsive shows the wordmark at 1440 and the symbol at 390, inside an app shell and outside one; resizing across the breakpoint with focus on the brand keeps focus on it.

behavior.text: THE app bar SHALL expose the brand as one link to brandHref named by brandLabel — or, WHILE brandHref is empty, as one image named by brandLabel — between the navigation item and the action items in reading order, and SHALL hide the brand's images from assistive technology, so that the product's name is read once whichever arrangement is shown. THE brand's link SHALL be a stop in the tab order and SHALL draw the focus indicator around its cell, in the shape comp.app-bar.brand.shape.
behavior.verify: Every brand fixture exposes one link named by brandLabel and no image; Tab goes navigation, brand, actions; the focus ring follows comp.app-bar.brand.shape; with brandHref empty the brand is one image named by brandLabel and no tab stop; axe passes in light and dark.

behavior.text: IF brandLayout names a value the app bar does not define THE app bar SHALL treat it as lockup and in debug builds report it; IF brand holds an image together with brand-symbol or brand-wordmark THE app bar SHALL show the image in brand alone and in debug builds report the others; IF the bar has a brand and brandLabel is empty, or a brand slot holds more than one image, THE app bar SHALL still draw what it holds and in debug builds report what is missing or extra.
behavior.verify: An unknown brandLayout draws a lockup and reports APB-23; brand with brand-symbol shows the brand image only and reports; a brand without brandLabel reports; two images in one slot render and report.

behavior.text: WHILE the brand is a lockup THE app bar SHALL draw the symbol comp.app-bar.brand.lockup.symbol.size high, which is the wordmark's height (comp.app-bar.brand.wordmark.height) unless a design system sets it apart, so that the symbol and the wordmark stand at one height; a symbol shown alone keeps comp.app-bar.brand.symbol.size.
behavior.verify: small-brand-lockup: the symbol's box is as high as the wordmark's, within 0.5 px; small-brand-symbol, and small-brand-responsive in a compact window, draw the symbol brand.symbol.size high.

behavior.text: WHERE the product puts a control in context THE app bar SHALL place it at the start of the top row after the brand, at comp.app-bar.actions.gap from the brand's cell (from the navigation item WHILE no brand is drawn, and comp.app-bar.container.padding-inline from the start edge WHILE neither is), vertically centred in the row, with the title block after it at comp.app-bar.container.gap; SHALL NOT restyle it, as APB-11 says of the navigation and action items; and SHALL keep it in reading order after the brand and before the title block and the action items. Right-to-left layouts SHALL mirror the order.
behavior.verify: Test on the web: a bar with a navigation button, a wordmark and a Button in context draws the Button actions.gap after the brand's cell, centred on the row's centre line, and the actions still at the end; Tab goes navigation, brand, context, actions; without a brand the Button stands actions.gap after the navigation button, and without either container.padding-inline from the start edge; in rtl the order mirrors.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the navigation item, then to the brand's link, then to the control in context, then through the action items; the bar itself is not a tab stop.

accessibility.labeling: The title is the screen's heading (a level 1 heading on the web unless the product sets another level). The subtitle is read after it. The navigation and action items, and the control in context, are named by their own labels. The brand is one link to the product's first page named by brandLabel (the product's name), whichever of its images is shown; its images are hidden from assistive technology.
notes: The app bar has no role of its own and takes no input: its buttons are the product's icon-only Buttons, which meet the minimum target themselves (BTN-5). The bar is not a landmark, because only the product knows whether it is its page's banner; a product that wants one wraps the bar in its own header element.

The title is truncated rather than wrapped even at 200% text size: the bar's rows grow with the text, but a bar of several lines would push the screen's content away. The full title stays available to assistive technology.
Where both titles of a large bar are partly visible, only the expanded one is exposed, so the heading is never read twice.

web.name: tanrei-app-bar
web.notes: `title` is the `headline` property and attribute, because HTML's global `title` attribute would show a tooltip over the whole bar. `titleAlignment` is the `title-alignment` attribute. The slots are `navigation`, `context` and `actions`. A web-only `scroll-target` attribute names the id of the scrolling element to connect (default: the document's scrolling element; `none` connects nothing), from which the bar sets `scrolled` itself. A web-only `heading-level` (default 1) sets the title's heading level. Insets are `env(safe-area-inset-top|left|right)`. `dividerVisibility` is the `divider-visibility` attribute (`auto`, `always`, `scroll`); `auto` reads `--tanrei-comp-app-bar-outline-visibility` from the cascade with a style query, and where the browser has none the bar writes the name it read on its container when it renders. navigation.name: tanrei-button
navigation.notes: An icon-only `<tanrei-button>` child with `slot="navigation"`; the glyph is its content.

action.name: tanrei-button
action.notes: An icon-only `<tanrei-button>` child with `slot="actions"`; the glyph is its content.

swiftui.name: TanreiAppBar
swiftui.notes: `TanreiAppBar(_ title:, subtitle:, size:, titleAlignment:, isScrolled: Bool? = nil) { navigation } actions: { … }`, placed with `.safeAreaInset(edge: .top)` in a `NavigationStack` whose system bar is hidden; the system bar's heights, title font and edge cannot be set from the tokens. Hiding it must not lose the interactive back swipe: the implementation keeps it working. The connected scroll view is the one marked `.tanreiAppBarScrollSource()`, applied after the `.safeAreaInset` that holds the bar (the inset's content sees only the environment where the inset is applied); it connects on iOS 18 and macOS 15 and later. `isScrolled: nil` follows it, a value overrides it. Not yet: the title's letter-spacing by the script of its text (APB-5, PRS-20). Not built on this platform yet: `dividerVisibility` (auto, always, scroll; APB-18) — the bar still draws its bottom edge from its condition's outline color, as `scroll` does. Not built on this platform yet: the brand (`brandHref`, `brandLabel`, `brandLayout` and its slots, APB-19 to APB-24). Not built on this platform yet: the context slot (APB-25).

navigation.name: TanreiButton
navigation.notes: An icon-only `TanreiButton` in the `navigation` view builder.

action.name: TanreiButton
action.notes: An icon-only `TanreiButton` in the `actions` view builder.

compose.name: TanreiAppBar
compose.notes: Compose idiom (as `TopAppBar`): `TanreiAppBar(title, navigationIcon = { … }, actions = { … }, subtitle, size, titleAlignment, scrollBehavior, windowInsets)`. `scrollBehavior` (`TanreiAppBarDefaults.pinnedScrollBehavior()` for small, `.collapseScrollBehavior()` for large) is connected with `Modifier.nestedScroll(scrollBehavior.nestedScrollConnection)`, and its state carries scrolled and the collapse; without one the bar is flat and expanded, and a state created with a given offset draws the scrolled fixtures. `windowInsets` defaults to the status bars plus the horizontal display cutout. Not yet: the title's letter-spacing by the script of its text (APB-5, PRS-20). Not built on this platform yet: `dividerVisibility` (auto, always, scroll; APB-18) — the bar still draws its bottom edge from its condition's outline color, as `scroll` does. Not built on this platform yet: the brand (`brandHref`, `brandLabel`, `brandLayout` and its slots, APB-19 to APB-24). Not built on this platform yet: the context slot (APB-25).

flutter.name: TanreiAppBar
flutter.notes: Flutter idiom (as `AppBar` and `SliverAppBar.large`): `TanreiAppBar` is a `PreferredSizeWidget` for `Scaffold.appBar`, with `leading`, `actions`, `title` (a String), `subtitle`, `size` and `centerTitle` (true for center). `scrolledUnder: null` follows the `ScrollNotification`s of the scaffold's body, as `AppBar`'s scrolled-under state does; a bool overrides it. A large bar that collapses is `TanreiSliverAppBar` inside a `CustomScrollView`. Insets through `SafeArea`/`MediaQuery.padding`. Not yet: the title's letter-spacing by the script of its text (APB-5, PRS-20). Not built on this platform yet: `dividerVisibility` (auto, always, scroll; APB-18) — the bar still draws its bottom edge from its condition's outline color, as `scroll` does. Not built on this platform yet: the brand (`brandHref`, `brandLabel`, `brandLayout` and its slots, APB-19 to APB-24). Not built on this platform yet: the context slot (APB-25).

action.name: TanreiButton
action.notes: An icon-only `TanreiButton` in the bar's `actions:` list.

react-native.name: AppBar
react-native.notes: `navigation` and `actions` are React nodes (an icon-only `Button`, and a fragment of up to three). The scroll connection is a hook: `const scroll = useAppBarScroll()` gives `scroll.onScroll` for a `ScrollView` or `FlatList` and `scroll.state` for the bar's `scrollState` prop, which sets scrolled and the collapse; without it the bar draws what `scrolled` says. Insets come from the bar's own `insets` prop, side by side, falling back to `TanreiProvider`'s `insets`; the package takes no safe-area dependency, and a product that uses `react-native-safe-area-context` passes its `useSafeAreaInsets()` to either. Not yet: the title's letter-spacing by the script of its text (APB-5, PRS-20). Not built on this platform yet: `dividerVisibility` (auto, always, scroll; APB-18) — the bar still draws its bottom edge from its condition's outline color, as `scroll` does. Not built on this platform yet: the brand (`brandHref`, `brandLabel`, `brandLayout` and its slots, APB-19 to APB-24). Not built on this platform yet: the context slot (APB-25).
